scenes.title: Count the two ticket colours
scenes.narration: A ticket envelope holds twenty tickets. For every blue ticket there are three yellow tickets. How many tickets of each colour are inside? Choose a group that uses both clues.

scenes.title: Unfold five matching groups
scenes.narration: Put one blue ticket beside three yellow tickets. That makes a group of four. Twenty tickets make five complete groups. Count five blue tickets and fifteen yellow tickets. Fifteen is three times five, and the envelope holds twenty.

scenes.title: Price a bundle in points
scenes.narration: At the next window, a plain ticket is worth one point and a star ticket is worth four points. Seven tickets together are worth nineteen points. How many carry a star? Try making all seven plain first.

scenes.title: Change one ticket at a time
scenes.narration: Seven plain tickets would give seven points. The bundle needs twelve more. Replace one plain ticket with a star. You gain three points, because the old ticket was already worth one. Four replacements supply twelve points. Four stars and three plain tickets make nineteen.

scenes.title: Sort three kinds of travel ticket
scenes.narration: A train sold sixteen tickets for thirty six seats. A ticket covers one seat, two seats or four seats. Just as many two seat tickets as four seat tickets were sold. Find the three ticket counts.

scenes.title: Match the extra seats
scenes.narration: Give every ticket one seat first. That accounts for sixteen seats and leaves twenty extra seats. Match each two seat ticket with a four seat ticket. Above the first seat, the pair adds one plus three extra seats. Twenty divided by four gives five pairs.

scenes.title: Audit both columns of the ledger
scenes.narration: Five two seat tickets and five four seat tickets account for ten tickets. The remaining six are single tickets. Now check the seats. Six singles, ten seats from the doubles and twenty seats from the fours make thirty six. Each extra group of four was forced, so the counts are unique.

scenes.title: Catch a report that cannot balance
scenes.narration: Three stalls report their ticket counts in pairs. The three pair totals are twelve, fifteen and twenty. Could every report be right? Adding all three counts each stall twice. Yet the reports add to forty seven, an odd number. Twice a whole number must be even. At least one report is wrong.
